content.text: Sb-rich compositions work best so far (0.70 is highest). I'm checking the phases with XRD before I spend the last EQE measurement.

input.rationale: Of the five compositions measured (Sb 0.28, 0.49, 0.70, 0.75, 0.80), index 20 (Sb 0.70) had the highest EQE at 0.00377%. Photoactivity only appears on the Sb-rich side and drops at 0.75 (0.00228%) and 0.80 (0.00159%). XRD at 0.61, 0.70 and 0.75 shows peaks near Q≈1.92, 2.48 and 3.68 Å⁻¹. These look like rutile but were not matched to reference patterns. The peak at 5.33 is probably the Pt substrate. The optimum seems to lie near Sb 0.65–0.70, close to CrSb2O6 (0.667).

rejected.reason: 0.00228%, lower than Sb 0.70 even though its rutile-like XRD peaks were strongest

content.text:
I submitted index 20 (Sb fraction 0.70). It had the highest EQE of the five compositions I measured, 0.00377%, though every signal on this line is very small. I used all 5 EQE measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | 0.28 | −0.0004 |
| 13 | 0.49 | −0.0003 |
| **20** | **0.70** | **0.00377** |
| 22 | 0.75 | 0.00228 |
| 24 | 0.80 | 0.00159 |

- **Where the activity is:** Samples at Sb 0.49 and below gave essentially zero. The response appears only on the Sb-rich side, peaks at 0.70 and falls off above that.
- **XRD:** I measured indices 17, 20 and 22 (Sb 0.61, 0.70, 0.75). All three show strong peaks at Q ≈ 1.92, 2.48 and 3.68 Å⁻¹, which I read as a rutile-type phase. The strongest peak (5.33) is probably the Pt substrate. I didn't run the tool that matches these peaks against reference structures, so the phase identification is not confirmed.
- **Last measurement:** I spent the final EQE on index 22 because its XRD peaks were strongest. It came in lower than index 20, so that bet didn't pay off.
- **Main gap:** Sb 0.61–0.63 (indices 17 and 18) was never EQE-measured. The Gaussian-process model predicted a lower average there than index 20's result, but with wide uncertainty. The true optimum could sit slightly below 0.70, which is near CrSb₂O₆ (Sb 0.667).
